title: Two-out-of-three coherent devissage on a Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and use algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], with module direct image and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Locally Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]; Noetherian means additionally quasi-compact and quasi-separated (quasi-compact diagonal). Coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $X$ be Noetherian and let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Suppose (0) $\mathcal P(0)$; (1) in every short exact sequence of coherent modules, if two terms have $\mathcal P$, so does the third; (2) for coherent $F$ and every integer $r\geq1$, $\mathcal P(F^{\oplus r})$ implies $\mathcal P(F)$; (3) for every reduced closed subspace $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with nonempty irreducible point space, there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $M$ such that $\mathcal P(M)$ and $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X}(M)=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$. Here a closed immersion is representable by closed immersions of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], reduced means reduced on etale charts, irreducible means not a union of two proper closed subsets, and the point topology is [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The annihilator consists of the local sections of the structure sheaf killing every local section of the module; its equality with this kernel says that the scheme theoretic support of $M$ is exactly $Z$. Then $\mathcal P(F)$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$.

source.place: Tag 08AN (lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological-variant), with the zero-object hypothesis explicit so the empty algebraic space is included.

proof.text: We use coherent modules throughout. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian], kernels, cokernels, finite direct sums and extensions of coherent modules are coherent. By [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], the structure module, quasi-coherent ideals, their quotients and quasi-coherent submodules of coherent modules are coherent and have closed support. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules] makes $Z$ Noetherian, preserves coherence under $i_*$ and identifies supports under the closed inclusion. Moreover [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules] makes $i_*$ exact on quasi-coherent modules. Thus every exact sequence below is a short exact sequence of coherent modules on $X$ after pushforward.

Check the support hypothesis needed for the witness. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be reduced closed, $J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, and let $M$ be coherent with $\operatorname{Ann}(M)=J$. Since $JM=0$, [lem-sfb-space-coherent-support-ideal-power] gives $\operatorname{Supp}(M)\subseteq|Z|$. Conversely put $T=\operatorname{Supp}(M)$, closed by [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], and give $T$ its reduced closed subspace structure $W$ by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]. Its defining ideal $L$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules]. The same ideal-power lemma gives $L^nM=0$ for some $n\geq1$ (increase the exponent if necessary), so $L^n\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}(M)=J$. On any affine scheme chart this inclusion implies $V(J)\subseteq V(L^n)=V(L)$: a prime containing $J$ contains each $n$th power from $L$ and hence $L$. Therefore $|Z|\subseteq T$. This proves $\operatorname{Supp}(M)=|Z|$ without replacing scheme-theoretic support by set-theoretic support as a hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 08AN, witness in the third proof paragraph; Tag 07UK (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), applied in both directions; reduced closed support from Tag 03IQ.

proof.text: We will also use the following elementary consequence of [lem-sfb-space-power-ideal-kills] on a nonempty reduced Noetherian closed subspace $Z$. If a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $A\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ had $Z(A)=|Z|$, that lemma applied to the coherent structure module would give $A^n=0$. The case $n=0$ forces $\mathcal O_Z=0$, contradicting nonemptiness; for $n>0$ every local section $a$ of $A$ has $a^n=0$, so reducedness forces $A=0$, again a contradiction. Hence $Z(A)$ is proper closed. If a coherent module $B$ is killed by $A$, the same lemma with exponent $1$ gives $\operatorname{Supp}(B)\subseteq Z(A)$. Coherence of the structure module needed here is [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support].

source.place: Tag 08AN, final proof paragraph, proper support of ideal quotients; Tag 07UK (lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf), with the reducedness calculation written out.

proof.text: Suppose some ideal pushforward $i_*A$ fails $\mathcal P$, with $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ reduced closed and $|Z|$ nonempty irreducible, and $A\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ quasi-coherent. Let $\mathcal T$ be the family of the corresponding closed subsets $|Z|$. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-topology] it has a minimal member $T=|Z|$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support] ensures that a given closed subset determines its reduced subspace, so minimality says: on every nonempty irreducible reduced closed subspace $Z'$ with $|Z'|\subsetneq T$, every quasi-coherent ideal pushforward has $\mathcal P$. In particular the zero ideal cannot witness failure, since $\mathcal P(0)$ and pushforward of zero is zero.

source.place: Tag 08AN (lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological-variant), first two proof paragraphs: the minimal bad reduced irreducible closed subspace.

proof.text: Every coherent $H$ on $X$ with $\operatorname{Supp}(H)\subsetneq T$ now has $\mathcal P$. Indeed apply the support-controlled filtration of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-ideal-filtration]. Each nonzero factor is $(i_j)_*A_j$ on a nonempty irreducible reduced closed subspace whose underlying subset lies in $\operatorname{Supp}(H)\subsetneq T$. Minimality from step 4 gives $\mathcal P$ for every factor. Starting with $\mathcal P(0)$, apply hypothesis (1) to $0\to H_{j-1}\to H_j\to H_j/H_{j-1}\to0$ successively. When $H$ has empty support the cited filtration has length zero and gives $H=0$.

source.place: Tag 08AN, third proof paragraph, applying Tag 07UR (lemma-coherent-filter) to coherent modules with proper support.

proof.text: Choose the witness $M$ of hypothesis (3) for this minimal $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$. It has $\mathcal P(M)$, is killed by $J=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, and has support $T$ by step 2. Apply [lem-sfb-space-reduced-support-generic-ideal-inclusion] to obtain $r\geq1$, a nonzero coherent ideal $K\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, and an injection $\alpha:i_*(K^{\oplus r})\hookrightarrow M$ with coherent cokernel $Q$ of support strictly contained in $T$. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules], $i_*K$ is coherent. Also $i_*(K^{\oplus r})\cong(i_*K)^{\oplus r}$: finite direct sums of module sheaves are finite products, and taking a finite tuple of sections commutes with the defining direct-image limit. This uses only the direct-image universal property of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors].

source.place: Tag 08AN, third proof paragraph, applying Tag 07UQ (lemma-prepare-filter-irreducible) to the chosen witness.

proof.text: Step 5 gives $\mathcal P(Q)$, and the witness has $\mathcal P(M)$. Apply hypothesis (1) to $0\to i_*(K^{\oplus r})\xrightarrow{\alpha}M\to Q\to0$ to obtain $\mathcal P(i_*(K^{\oplus r}))$. Under the finite-sum identification of step 6, hypothesis (2), with $r\geq1$ and the coherent module $i_*K$, gives $\mathcal P(i_*K)$.

source.place: Tag 08AN, third proof paragraph, two-out-of-three followed by reflection from a positive finite direct sum.

proof.text: Let $A\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ be any other quasi-coherent ideal. If $A=0$, its pushforward has $\mathcal P$ by hypothesis (0), so suppose $A\ne0$. Set $C=K\cap A$. By [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support], $K$ and $A$ are coherent. The intersection is the kernel of $K\to\mathcal O_Z/A$, so [lem-sfb-space-coherent-abelian] makes $C$, $K/C$ and $A/C$ coherent. Products give $A(K/C)=0$ and $K(A/C)=0$, since $AK\subseteq K\cap A=C$. Step 3 therefore puts their supports in the proper closed subsets $Z(A)$ and $Z(K)$ of $|Z|$, respectively. By [lem-sfb-space-closed-coherent-modules], the coherent modules $i_*(K/C)$ and $i_*(A/C)$ have support strictly contained in $T$. Step 5 gives $\mathcal P$ for both of them.

source.place: Tag 08AN, final proof paragraph: intersection of the two ideals and proper support of both quotients, with the annihilating products explicit.

proof.text: By exactness of closed pushforward [lem-sfb-space-closed-immersion-quasi-coherent-modules], the two intersection sequences give $0\to i_*C\to i_*K\to i_*(K/C)\to0$ and $0\to i_*C\to i_*A\to i_*(A/C)\to0$. All terms are coherent by steps 1 and 8. The first sequence, step 7 and step 8 give $\mathcal P(i_*C)$ by hypothesis (1). The second sequence then gives $\mathcal P(i_*A)$. This holds for every quasi-coherent ideal $A$ on $Z$, contradicting the choice of $T$. Consequently the family $\mathcal T$ of step 4 is empty.

source.place: Tag 08AN, final proof paragraph, the two exact intersection sequences and the contradiction to minimality.

proof.text: Finally take any coherent $F$ on $X$ and its filtration from [lem-sfb-space-coherent-ideal-filtration]. Since $\mathcal T$ is empty, every ideal-pushforward factor has $\mathcal P$. Induction along this finite filtration using hypothesis (1), starting with hypothesis (0), gives $\mathcal P(F)$. The length-zero filtration covers $F=0$ and the empty space. This is the finite-filtration argument behind Tag 07US, rather than a new node restating the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 08AN, first proof sentence reducing to Tag 07US (lemma-property-initial), expanded using Tag 07UR (lemma-coherent-filter).

proof_origin.place: Tag 08AN (lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological-variant), complete proof; the two uses of Tag 07US are expanded using the existing support-controlled Tag 07UR filtration.
